description: Five reports provided information to Council.
City will research provincial and Western Canadian rules for shelters near childcare.

chips.text: Councillor Dubois emphasized balancing safety for vulnerable children and homeless individuals.
90 children aged 18 months to five years at YWCA childcare facility.
Whether the provincial Ministry of Education has input on shelter proximity to daycares is unclear.

speakers.name: Sara Wheelwright
speakers.summary: Sara Wheelwright addressed Committee expressing concerns about locating the proposed drop‑in centre near a childcare facility, citing observed safety issues in the area, and urged Council to formalize separation distance requirements and...
said: Proximity matters; separation distance should apply to daycares, not just schools.
Proposed 130 Idylwyld drop-in is 30 steps from YWCA daycare.
Witnessed drug deals, paraphernalia near proposed site and daycare playground.

speakers.name: Shawna Nelson
speakers.summary: Shawna Nelson addressed Committee emphasizing the need to formalize and expand separation distance requirements, citing impacts observed near existing sites.
said: Formalize separation distance into a bylaw; current approach is incomplete.
Drop-in centers have similar or greater impacts; need consistent rules.
Expand 250m buffer to daycares, child-serving facilities, and senior living.

description: Increases community safety patrols at Avenue C and public washrooms.
Funds higher intensity security patrols for the rest of 2026.
Addresses increased social disorder near service sites.

chips.text: City Manager stated province expects city to fund external community safety costs.
Residents of Rumley Distinctive Lofts and King George Condominium are affected.
Councillor Timon's question about Riversdale BID's role in safety was unanswered.
Delegate urged maximum funding for safety, citing Pacific Avenue shelter's success.
Shelter and drop-in centre users are directly supported by safety measures.
City Manager committed to site-specific cost reporting for future shelters.

speakers.name: Timothy Cain
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Community Safety Update - Service Levels for Ave C
said: Past emergency wellness centre caused significant crime and social disorder.
Coordinated safety plan at Pacific Avenue shelter has been highly effective.
Flexible, well-resourced safety plans enable supportive housing and community safety.
